title: LabStart Fellowship 2027: Launch Your Climate Tech Startup With Funding, Mentorship and Access to U.S. Research Technologies
summary: The LabStart Fellowship 2027 is inviting entrepreneurs and aspiring founders with a passion for climate technology and entrepreneurship to apply for its next cohort. The program is designed to help entrepreneurs turn promising climate technologies and research into viable startups by providing funding, training, mentorship, access to technologies, and connections across the climate innovation ecosystem. Applications for the 2027 cohort are currently open , with a deadline of October 9, 2026 . LabStart focuses on bridging the gap between promising technologies developed in research laboratories and their commercialization in the market. Its program connects entrepreneurs with technologies, researchers, technology-transfer offices, industry experts, investors, and other stakeholders who can help transform an early-stage idea into a functioning climate technology company. What Is the LabStart Fellowship? The LabStart Fellowship is a climate technology entrepreneurship program designed to help founders move from an early-stage concept or technology opportunity toward launching a company. The program focuses particularly on deep climate technology , including technologies emerging from research laboratories and universities. Rather than requiring every applicant to arrive with a fully developed company, LabStart describes several situations in which its program can be useful. These include entrepreneurs who: Want to start a climate technology company but have not yet identified the ideal technology or business opportunity. Have identified a promising technology but need help obtaining a license. Have not yet raised capital for a specific product or technology. Are exploring a new market or innovative climate solution. Want to spin a technology out of a laboratory or university. Are looking for technologies to commercialize but have not yet identified the right market. The fellowship therefore focuses on helping entrepreneurs navigate the difficult journey between technology development, commercialization, company formation, and market entry . LabStart s Approach to Climate Technology LabStart s model is based on the idea that significant climate innovations can remain underdeveloped or under-commercialized when researchers do not have the entrepreneurial expertise, networks, capital, or commercialization pathways required to bring those technologies to market. The organization works with research laboratories, universities, technology-transfer offices, industry partners, and entrepreneurs to help close this gap. Its approach includes: Identifying promising climate technologies. Connecting those technologies with entrepreneurs. Helping founders evaluate market opportunities. Supporting intellectual-property and licensing processes. Providing entrepreneurship training. Connecting founders with mentors. Providing funding. Preparing companies for future investment and accelerator opportunities. What Does the LabStart Fellowship Provide? The current LabStart program provides a combination of funding, training, mentorship, technology access, and networks . The official program page describes the fellowship as a 12-month program with access to capital, capacity building, networks, and technology commercialization support. 1. Access to Capital LabStart provides milestone-based funding to support founders during the early stages of building their companies. The current program materials describe: $100,000 milestone-based funding on the program page. Full-time funding intended to give founders financial stability while focusing on their startups. Recent LabStart communications about the 2027–28 cohort have also referred to up to $125,000 in direct and in-kind funding , including support associated with the Discovery and Launch phases. Because the figures differ across current LabStart materials, applicants should check the latest program and application materials for the exact funding structure applicable to Cohort 2027. 2. Climate Tech Entrepreneurship Training Fellows receive training focused on climate technology entrepreneurship. The curriculum is designed to help participants understand how to: Evaluate emerging technologies. Identify market opportunities. Build a commercially viable business. Develop a climate technology startup. Navigate intellectual property. Commercialize research. Grow a company sustainably. The program s curriculum is developed and delivered by FRACTAL , whose leaders have experience working with climate technology companies. 3. Expert Mentorship Participants receive mentorship from experienced climate entrepreneurs and deep-tech professionals. The mentorship component can help founders understand the practical challenges associated with: Startup development Technology commercialization Market validation Fundraising Intellectual property Business strategy Company growth LabStart describes its mentor and partner network as an important part of helping entrepreneurs navigate the path from laboratory innovation to market. 4. Access to Research Technologies One of the defining features of LabStart is its connection to research institutions. Fellows can receive access to technologies developed through U.S. research institutions and laboratories and can work with researchers and technology-transfer offices to explore commercialization opportunities. This can be particularly relevant to founders who want to build a company around a technology that has already undergone significant scientific development but still needs an entrepreneur and commercialization strategy. 5. Intellectual Property and Licensing Support Commercializing laboratory research often requires navigating intellectual-property rights and licensing agreements. LabStart provides guidance on areas such as: Initial technology licenses Copyright agreements Technology development plans Technology-transfer processes Licensing negotiations Commercialization pathways The program states that it can also provide financial assistance for initial licensing agreements and consultations. 6. Industry and Investor Networks LabStart fellows gain access to a network involving: Climate innovators Industry leaders Investors Potential partners Research institutions Technology-transfer offices Incubators Accelerators These connections can be valuable when founders begin looking for customers, investment, partnerships, technical expertise, or additional startup support. Who Is LabStart Looking For? The 2027 application page identifies several characteristics associated with the type of entrepreneur LabStart is seeking. Passion for Climate and Entrepreneurship Applicants should demonstrate genuine interest in both: Climate solutions; and Entrepreneurship. The program is intended for people who want to create businesses capable of addressing climate-related challenges. Willingness to Launch a Company Full Time Applicants should be willing and ready to dedicate themselves to launching a company full time . This is an important commitment because LabStart s program is designed around founders actively building their ventures rather than participating casually alongside another primary commitment. Nontraditional and First-Time Founders LabStart explicitly welcomes people who may not follow the traditional startup-founder profile. The application page identifies: Nontraditional founders Women BIPOC founders First-time founders as groups represented in the type of entrepreneurial community LabStart seeks to support. Previous startup experience is not necessarily required. LabStart s earlier fellowship announcement specifically stated that previous startup experience was not required and that the program was open to people who wanted to launch climate startups even if they had not yet identified the perfect idea. APPLY HERE The LabStart Application Journey The 2027 application process asks applicants to demonstrate several important elements of their background, experience, entrepreneurial thinking, and climate technology vision. Step 1: Background Applicants are asked to showcase their journey and explain the experiences that have contributed to their interest in climate innovation. This is an opportunity to demonstrate how personal, academic, professional, research, technical, or entrepreneurial experiences have shaped the applicant s interest in climate technology. Applicants should be able to explain: What experiences have influenced them. Why climate innovation matters to them. How their previous journey connects to entrepreneurship. What motivates them to build a climate-focused company. Step 2: Past Experience Applicants should demonstrate their existing expertise. This can involve explaining: Previous projects Technical skills Professional experience Research experience Industry knowledge Entrepreneurial experience Relevant scientific or engineering capabilities The purpose is to demonstrate what the applicant can bring to the development and commercialization of a climate technology. Step 3: Startup Idea Applicants must explain their startup vision. This involves describing a proposed solution to a climate-related problem and explaining how the idea could contribute to addressing climate change. Applicants should be prepared to communicate: The problem they want to solve. The technology or innovation behind their proposed solution. Who could use the solution. Why the problem matters. How the solution could create value. What makes the approach potentially different or useful. Step 4: Choose Your Challenge The program also provides applicants with an opportunity to explore a curated selection of high-potential, licensable technologies. These technologies are identified and reviewed by LabStart s laboratory partners and stakeholders. Applicants can consider these technologies when developing their commercialization strategy or can propose other institutions, technologies, needs, or market gaps they believe should be addressed. This means applicants do not necessarily have to approach the program with a single fully developed technology already in hand. Characteristics LabStart Values LabStart identifies several traits that it looks for in prospective fellows. Scientific Literacy Applicants should have the ability to evaluate the potential impact and market opportunity associated with a technology. Scientific literacy does not simply mean understanding scientific concepts. It also involves being able to connect technology with real-world problems and commercial opportunities. Entrepreneurial Spirit Entrepreneurs need the ability to communicate a vision, tell a compelling story, experiment, and make decisions while managing uncertainty and risk. LabStart identifies entrepreneurial spirit as an important characteristic for fellows. Grit and Tenacity Building a climate technology company can involve significant challenges. LabStart therefore looks for people who are willing to persist when they encounter: Technical obstacles Market challenges Funding difficulties Licensing barriers Business setbacks Other roadblocks Technological Motivation Applicants should have a genuine interest in particular technologies or technology fields that could inspire the creation of a new business. This can be connected to a specific scientific discipline, engineering area, energy technology, materials technology, climate solution, or another relevant field. Authenticity and Coachability LabStart values founders who understand their current position and remain open to constructive feedback. Being coachable can be important because early-stage entrepreneurs frequently need to adapt their assumptions based on information from: Mentors Customers Researchers Investors Industry professionals Team members Collaborative Mindset Climate technology commercialization often involves scientists, engineers, entrepreneurs, investors, researchers, customers, and other stakeholders. LabStart therefore seeks people who can work effectively with diverse teams and make use of collective expertise. LabStart s Two-Phase Approach Recent LabStart communications describe the fellowship as having a Discovery Phase and a Launch Phase . Discovery Phase The Discovery Phase is designed to help entrepreneurs explore technologies and determine whether there is a viable technology-market opportunity. The earlier fellowship structure described this phase as a four-month, part-time program , with funding and training designed to help participants identify emerging laboratory technologies and evaluate their market potential. Launch Phase The Launch Phase is focused on moving from exploration toward company creation. The earlier structure described the Launch Phase as a year-long, full-time program , with significant funding, training, and expert support to develop the solution and build the company. The current program page similarly describes a 12-month training and support structure and emphasizes the expectation that fellows work full time on launching their companies. Applicants should check the current Cohort 2027 application materials for the precise phase dates and funding terms. What Happens During the Program? LabStart s curriculum is focused on helping entrepreneurs develop the capabilities needed to take climate technologies from research environments into the market. Core areas include: Evaluating emerging laboratory technologies. Understanding market potential. Identifying customer needs. Developing a business model. Understanding intellectual property. Navigating licensing. Developing a commercialization strategy. Building a climate technology company. Preparing for future investment. Developing relationships with investors, industry partners, laboratories, and other stakeholders. The goal is not simply to create an idea but to help founders develop a pathway toward a viable climate venture. LabStart s Climate Technology Focus LabStart focuses on technologies capable of addressing significant climate and sustainability challenges. Its fellows and alumni have worked across areas including: Energy Renewable energy Energy storage Advanced materials Industrial decarbonization Carbon reduction Circular materials Recycling Grid modernization Agriculture Sustainable manufacturing Infrastructure Climate adaptation The program s current fellows include entrepreneurs working on technologies related to areas such as methane reduction, solar energy, demand-response software, critical minerals, sustainable materials, biofuels, and grid modernization. Examples of Climate Innovation Supported by LabStart LabStart s fellowship community illustrates the range of climate technology ideas that can emerge from the program. Examples include: Carbon-negative methanol from methane emissions. Technologies designed to improve residential solar adoption. Demand-response software for vertical farming. Algae-based biofuels. Technologies addressing industrial plastics recycling. Low-carbon construction materials. Grid modernization solutions. Technologies addressing data-center sustainability. Solutions focused on industrial decarbonization. These examples demonstrate that climate technology is a broad field extending well beyond traditional renewable-energy businesses. Connection to U.S. Research Institutions A major component of LabStart s model is its connection to U.S. research laboratories and universities . The organization has worked with institutions including: National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL) Sandia National Laboratories Oak Ridge National Laboratory Pacific Northwest National Laboratory These partnerships help create pathways through which entrepreneurs can explore the commercialization of research and technology developed within the U.S. research ecosystem. Is Previous Startup Experience Required? No previous startup experience is required according to LabStart s previous fellowship announcement. The organization has explicitly highlighted opportunities for first-time founders and people who may not have followed traditional entrepreneurial paths. This means someone who has strong scientific, technical, research, professional, or industry experience but has never founded a company can still be considered within the program s target founder community. Is It Necessary to Already Have a Startup? Not necessarily. LabStart specifically describes situations where its program can support people who are still searching for the right technology or market opportunity. The program may therefore be relevant to someone who: Has a strong climate technology interest but no final startup idea. Has identified a technology but needs help commercializing it. Wants to build a company around laboratory research. Is looking for a technology to commercialize. Is exploring a new market. Has an early-stage company and is looking for a strategic technology or commercialization pathway. Full-Time Commitment A major expectation is the ability to work full time on launching the company . LabStart states that fellows commit to working full time on their company for the year and participating in approximately 6–8 hours per week of LabStart programming and events . Potential applicants should therefore consider whether they can make the required time commitment before applying. Information Sessions for Cohort 2027 LabStart has scheduled information sessions for applicants interested in learning more about the 2027 cohort. The application page lists: September 9 at 9:30 a.m. PT October 6 at 3:00 p.m. PT These sessions provide an opportunity for prospective applicants to learn more about the program and application process. Application Deadline Applications for the LabStart Cohort 2027 must be submitted by: October 9, 2026 The official LabStart application page currently lists October 9 as the application deadline. Applicants should submit their materials before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours. How to Apply Applicants can review the program details and submit an application through LabStart s official application process. Program information: LabStart Program Details Application: LabStart Application Page The program s application page provides the current Cohort 2027 information and links applicants to the application process. Key Details at a Glance Category Details Program LabStart Fellowship Cohort 2027 Focus Climate technology entrepreneurship Duration Approximately 12 months of program support Main objective Launch and commercialize climate technology startups Funding Current materials describe milestone-based funding; recent 2027 communications reference up to $125,000 in direct and in-kind funding Training Climate tech entrepreneurship and intellectual property fundamentals Mentorship Climate founders and deep-tech experts Technology access U.S. research institutions and laboratories Licensing support Yes Investor/industry networks Yes Full-time commitment Required Target founders Climate-focused entrepreneurs, including nontraditional and first-time founders Women/BIPOC Specifically encouraged/represented in the program s target community Application deadline October 9, 2026 Program information LabStart website Application LabStart application page Who Can Apply? The program is aimed at entrepreneurs and aspiring founders interested in launching climate technology companies . The current application materials indicate that suitable applicants should demonstrate: Passion for climate and entrepreneurship. Willingness to launch a company full time. Interest in commercializing climate technology. Relevant experience, expertise, or technical knowledge. Scientific literacy. Entrepreneurial spirit. Persistence and resilience. Motivation to work with technology. Openness to feedback and coaching. Ability to collaborate with diverse teams. The program specifically welcomes nontraditional founders, women, BIPOC founders, and first-time founders . Visit HERE to learn more about the LabStart Fellowship 2027 Geographic Eligibility LabStart s current program is centered on commercializing technologies from U.S. research laboratories and universities , and external descriptions of the 2027 fellowship identify the program region as the United States . The materials provided do not state a simple citizenship requirement such as U.S. citizens only. Therefore, nationality should not be described as an automatic eligibility requirement based solely on the available information. However, the program s focus on U.S. research institutions and the U.S. climate technology ecosystem means applicants should carefully review the current application form for any residency, location, work authorization, company formation, or other geographic requirements that may apply to Cohort 2027. For applicants outside the United States, including applicants from Africa or Zambia , the available public program information does not establish that they are automatically eligible. The application materials should be checked for the current cohort s specific geographic requirements before applying. Race and Demographic Eligibility LabStart s application materials specifically mention: Women BIPOC founders Nontraditional founders First-time founders as part of the founder community it seeks to support. This does not mean that the program is presented as being exclusively limited to those categories. Rather, LabStart states that it seeks to build diverse cohorts and specifically highlights these groups among the entrepreneurs it wants to support. The program s broader selection characteristics remain centered on climate passion, entrepreneurship, technological motivation, scientific literacy, resilience, coachability, and collaboration. Conclusion The LabStart Fellowship Cohort 2027 is designed for entrepreneurs who want to turn climate technology opportunities into real companies. The program combines funding, entrepreneurship training, expert mentorship, technology access, intellectual-property guidance, licensing support, and connections to investors and industry partners. A particularly distinctive aspect of the program is its focus on connecting entrepreneurs with research-based technologies from U.S. laboratories and universities . Rather than focusing solely on conventional startup ideas, LabStart works to identify promising technologies and help entrepreneurs develop commercialization pathways for them. The program is also designed to accommodate different founder journeys. Applicants do not necessarily need to be experienced startup founders, and LabStart explicitly highlights first-time and nontraditional founders, as well as women and BIPOC entrepreneurs, within the community it seeks to build. Successful participants are expected to make a significant commitment to the program, including working full time toward launching their company and participating in LabStart programming. The program is therefore intended for people who are ready to move beyond simply exploring entrepreneurship and toward actively building a climate technology venture. For Cohort 2027 , applications close on October 9, 2026 . Prospective applicants should review the latest LabStart program and application materials carefully, particularly regarding the current funding structure and any geographic or participation requirements, before submitting their application. title: SpaceX Intern Program 2026: Paid Internship Opportunities in Engineering, Software, and Business Operations
summary: The SpaceX Intern Program offers university students and graduate students the opportunity to gain hands-on experience while contributing to real projects in the aerospace and space technology industry. The year-round program provides opportunities across a wide range of engineering functions, software roles, and business operations , allowing interns to work alongside SpaceX employees on challenging projects. Unlike a traditional internship focused primarily on observation or classroom-style learning, SpaceX states that interns can receive substantial responsibility and play an important role in the company s work. Successful applicants typically demonstrate both strong academic performance and meaningful hands-on experience through extracurricular projects, university teams, previous employment, internships, or similar activities. About the SpaceX Intern Program SpaceX describes its internship program as an opportunity for students to contribute directly to the company s work in space exploration and its broader goal of making humanity a multiplanetary species. Interns can work across both technical and non-technical areas of the company. Depending on the specific position, responsibilities may involve designing, developing, testing, manufacturing, analyzing, researching, coordinating, or supporting business operations. The program is designed to provide students with practical experience that complements their university education. SpaceX emphasizes that interns are not simply observers. Interns can be given significant responsibilities and may contribute to projects alongside full-time employees. SpaceX Internship Opportunities SpaceX offers internship opportunities across multiple areas of the organization. 1. Engineering Engineering interns can participate in work involving the development of spaceflight hardware and related systems. Engineering internship responsibilities may include areas such as: Design Development Testing Manufacturing Engineering analysis Hardware development Hands-on technical projects The exact responsibilities depend on the specific engineering position and team. 2. Software Software internships are also available within the program. Students interested in software may have the opportunity to contribute to projects involving software development and other technical challenges associated with SpaceX operations. SpaceX notes that software internship applicants may include students enrolled in graduate programs by the beginning of employment. 3. Business Operations The program is not limited to engineering and software. SpaceX also offers opportunities in business operations , where interns contribute to the company s broader business objectives. These roles demonstrate that students from non-engineering disciplines can also find opportunities within the SpaceX Intern Program when they possess relevant skills and experience. Difference Between a SpaceX Intern and Graduate Engineer SpaceX distinguishes between its internship positions and graduate engineer positions. Internships Internships are available to technical and non-technical candidates who are currently enrolled at a four-year accredited university. For business operations and software roles , candidates may also be enrolled in a graduate program by the beginning of employment. Interns can contribute to actual company projects and gain hands-on professional experience. Graduate Engineer Positions Graduate engineer positions are specifically intended for engineering graduates. Candidates must have: Completed a bachelor s degree in engineering, physics, or mathematics; and Be enrolled in a graduate program by the beginning of employment. Graduate engineers work on actual space hardware development projects and are expected to work both independently and collaboratively. What Does SpaceX Look For in Intern Candidates? According to SpaceX, strong candidates typically have more than good academic results. The company highlights two important areas: Strong academic performance Significant hands-on extracurricular project experience This means students can strengthen their applications by demonstrating that they have actually applied what they have learned. For example, relevant experience could include: University engineering projects Student-led technical organizations Coding projects Design and manufacturing projects Research projects Business or entrepreneurial projects Team-based university initiatives Previous internships Relevant employment Other practical projects connected to the position SpaceX states that successful candidates for advanced internships and entry-level full-time positions often participate in student-driven projects involving designing, building, testing, or coding. For non-technical internship candidates, SpaceX looks for comparable hands-on project experience relevant to their particular field. When Are SpaceX Internships Available? One of the notable features of the SpaceX Intern Program is that opportunities are available year-round . Interns and graduate engineers must be available to work full time for a minimum of 12 weeks . The program operates across three main seasons: Spring January – April Summer May – August Fall September – December Students should therefore monitor SpaceX s careers website regularly because opportunities can be posted for different locations and seasons. SpaceX Internship Locations SpaceX lists internship and graduate engineer opportunities across multiple locations in the United States. Locations listed in the program information include: Bastrop, Texas Cape Canaveral, Florida Hawthorne, California Irvine, California McGregor, Texas Redmond, Washington Starbase, Texas Sunnyvale, California Vandenberg, California Washington, DC Bloomfield, Connecticut Long Beach, California Woodinville, Washington SpaceX notes that site availability varies by season , meaning not every location will necessarily have internship positions available during every internship period. Applicants should therefore check the individual internship listing for the location and term associated with each position. Can Master s and PhD Students Apply? Yes. SpaceX states that its Intern Program demographics are predominantly made up of upperclassmen and graduate students . Students pursuing master s or PhD-level education may therefore be eligible for appropriate internship opportunities. Students enrolled in engineering graduate programs may also qualify for graduate engineer positions, provided they meet the specific educational requirements. The precise eligibility requirements can vary depending on the position, so applicants should carefully review each individual job posting. Does SpaceX Recruit Only From Certain Universities? No. SpaceX states that there is no single set of universities or colleges from which it exclusively recruits . Instead, the company emphasizes the importance of what candidates have actually accomplished. For technical applicants, this can include participation in student-driven engineering groups where students design, build, test, or code projects. For non-technical applicants, comparable hands-on project experience in their respective fields can also be valuable. This means that attending a particular university is not presented as a requirement for applying to the program. Are International Students Eligible? International applicants face specific restrictions because SpaceX works with technologies subject to U.S. government export regulations. SpaceX states that, to comply with International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and other U.S. government space technology export regulations, applicants must fall into one of the following categories: U.S. citizens Lawful permanent residents of the United States Protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) Individuals who are eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State Therefore, being a university student outside the United States does not by itself establish eligibility. International applicants must meet the applicable authorization requirements for the particular position. Can F-1 Visa Students Receive Sponsorship? SpaceX specifically states that it cannot provide employment sponsorship to students holding F-1 visa status . Students currently studying in the United States under F-1 status should therefore take this restriction into account when assessing their eligibility. Because immigration and export-control requirements can be position-specific, applicants should also review the requirements stated in the individual internship posting. Is There a Minimum GPA Requirement? There is no minimum GPA requirement for the SpaceX Intern Program. However, SpaceX states that it has a preferred cumulative GPA of 3.5 or higher . This means that a GPA below 3.5 does not automatically prevent someone from applying according to the information provided, although academic performance remains part of the overall candidate profile. Applicants should also focus on demonstrating relevant projects, technical or professional experience, and their individual contributions to previous work. What Should You Include on Your SpaceX Internship Resume? SpaceX recommends that applicants provide specific information on their resumes. 1. University Information Include: University name Degree Major or majors Cumulative GPA Expected graduation date 2. Previous Experience Include relevant: Internships Co-ops Jobs Other professional experience Experience should be relevant to the particular internship wherever possible. 3. Project Experience SpaceX particularly encourages applicants to describe relevant project-team involvement. Your resume should communicate: The project you worked on Your role What you personally contributed The challenges you encountered What you accomplished Simply listing a project may not fully demonstrate your abilities. Applicants should make their individual contribution clear. SpaceX Internship Interview Process Candidates who are selected for interviews may go through several stages. SpaceX states that candidates may undergo technical phone screens . Depending on the specific team and position, candidates may also be required to complete: A quiz A project A programming test Other technical assessments The interview process can therefore vary depending on the position. APPLY HERE How Should Applicants Prepare for the Interview? SpaceX recommends that candidates be prepared to discuss their most significant technical achievements. Applicants should be able to explain: What project they worked on What problem they were trying to solve What their individual contribution was What challenges they encountered How they approached those challenges How they innovated How they improved or advanced the project What they learned from the experience A particularly important point is being able to distinguish your contribution from the work completed by the broader team. For example, rather than simply saying that you were part of a project, you should be prepared to explain exactly what you designed, developed, tested, researched, analyzed, organized, or improved. SpaceX also recommends that candidates understand the company s mission and be able to explain how that mission relates to their own skills. How Long Does the Recruitment Process Take? Applicants should be prepared for the recruitment process to take some time. SpaceX states that it receives a large volume of applications and cannot personally respond to every applicant. Recruiters will contact candidates who are selected for interviews. SpaceX also notes that recruiting for a particular internship or graduate engineer position can take up to six months . Applicants should therefore not necessarily interpret a lack of immediate communication as a final decision. Should You Reapply If You Are Not Selected? Yes. SpaceX encourages applicants who are not selected to continue applying for future opportunities. Because there are many applicants and a limited number of internship and graduate engineer positions, applicants may want to continue monitoring the careers page. SpaceX also recommends applying to multiple locations and internship terms to increase visibility and opportunities for consideration. However, each application should still be relevant to the applicant s qualifications and interests. Are SpaceX Internships Paid? Yes. SpaceX states that its internships and graduate engineer opportunities are paid . This makes the program different from unpaid internships where students may receive professional experience without financial compensation. The supplied program information does not state a specific internship salary or hourly rate, so applicants should check the individual job posting for compensation details where available. Can SpaceX Internships Count Toward University Course Credit? Yes, potentially. SpaceX states that internships and graduate engineer positions can be used to satisfy course credit at the discretion of the student s university . This means the decision ultimately depends on the student s institution and its academic requirements. Students who need an internship for academic credit should therefore consult their university or academic department before assuming that the SpaceX position will automatically satisfy their requirements. Restrictions on Internship Work and Academic Reports Because SpaceX interns may work with proprietary, sensitive, and/or ITAR-controlled projects, there are restrictions on publicly presenting internship work. SpaceX states that it cannot allow interns to create presentations, papers, or reports about the work they complete at the company when the work involves these protected areas. Where necessary, SpaceX can confirm the dates of employment to a university or instructor and provide a brief overview of the type of experience provided through the internship. Students who need to submit a detailed internship report as part of their academic program should therefore consider this restriction before accepting a position and discuss the requirements with their university. SpaceX Intern Program: Key Details Detail Information Opportunity SpaceX Intern Program Organization SpaceX Opportunity type Paid internship / graduate engineer opportunities Fields Engineering, software, business operations and related functions Availability Year-round Duration Minimum 12 weeks, full time Seasons Spring, Summer, Fall Locations Multiple locations across the United States Graduate students Eligible for applicable internship opportunities GPA No minimum; 3.5+ preferred International applicants Subject to U.S. export-control/ITAR eligibility F-1 sponsorship Not provided Course credit Possible, subject to university discretion Deadline No single program-wide deadline stated Application Through individual SpaceX internship job postings Application Process SpaceX does not provide one universal application deadline for the entire Intern Program. Instead, applicants should search the company s careers website for currently available internship positions and apply to positions that match their qualifications, field, preferred location, and available season. Because opportunities are posted throughout the year, students should monitor the internship listings regularly. Apply for current SpaceX internship opportunities: View SpaceX Internships Important Eligibility Considerations for International Applicants For students applying from outside the United States, eligibility is particularly important. The program information does not state that all international students are eligible simply because they meet the academic requirements. Instead, SpaceX states that applicants must satisfy applicable U.S. government space technology export regulations, including ITAR requirements. Therefore, applicants from countries outside the United States should carefully review the eligibility requirements of each individual position and determine whether they can obtain the necessary authorization. The supplied information does not provide a list of specific countries whose citizens are automatically eligible. Who Can Apply? The opportunity is primarily aimed at students currently enrolled in higher education , including: Undergraduate students at four-year accredited universities Upperclassmen Graduate students Master s students PhD students, where applicable Engineering students who meet graduate engineer requirements Students pursuing technical disciplines Students pursuing non-technical disciplines relevant to business operations Students with relevant hands-on project experience Academic Requirements For standard internships: Candidates should be currently enrolled at a four-year accredited university. Business operations and software applicants may also be enrolled in a graduate program by the start of employment. For graduate engineer positions: Candidates must have completed a bachelor s degree in engineering, physics, or mathematics. They must be enrolled in a graduate program by the beginning of employment. There is no stated minimum GPA, although a cumulative GPA of 3.5 or higher is preferred . Nationality and Geographic Eligibility SpaceX states that applicants must satisfy applicable U.S. government export-control requirements. Eligible individuals must be one of the following: U.S. citizen U.S. lawful permanent resident Protected individual under the specified U.S. law An individual eligible to obtain the necessary U.S. Department of State authorization The supplied information does not identify a specific list of African, European, Asian, or other countries whose nationals can automatically apply. For applicants from countries such as Zambia , eligibility should therefore be determined based on the applicable authorization requirements rather than assuming that nationality alone qualifies or disqualifies an applicant. Visit HERE to learn more the SpaceX Intern Program 2026 Deadline No single program-wide deadline is stated. SpaceX operates its internship program throughout the year, with Spring, Summer, and Fall opportunities. Individual internship positions may have their own application timelines, so applicants should check the specific job listing for the position and term they are interested in. Conclusion The SpaceX Intern Program provides university and graduate students with an opportunity to gain paid, full-time, hands-on experience in one of the world s major space technology companies. Opportunities span engineering, software, business operations, and other functions, meaning the program is not limited exclusively to engineering students. SpaceX places considerable emphasis on practical experience, academic performance, and evidence that applicants have actively contributed to projects. Students should therefore look beyond their GPA and build a strong record of relevant projects, extracurricular activities, internships, employment, research, coding, design, or other hands-on work. The program is available across multiple U.S. locations and operates during Spring, Summer, and Fall seasons, with a minimum commitment of 12 weeks. Internships are paid and may potentially count toward university course credit. For international students, however, U.S. export-control and ITAR requirements are a major eligibility consideration, and SpaceX does not provide employment sponsorship for students on F-1 visas. Applicants should carefully examine the eligibility requirements attached to each individual position before applying. Students interested in pursuing an internship should regularly monitor the SpaceX careers page because opportunities are available throughout the year and individual positions may have different requirements and timelines. title: Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship: Practical Training and Mentorship in Arts and Culture Consulting
summary: The Lynette A. Turner Pathways to Consulting Fellowship , offered by AMS Planning Research, is an opportunity designed to increase the participation of people from historically underrepresented groups in the arts and culture consulting field. The fellowship provides practical professional training, mentorship, and exposure to consulting work involving arts organizations, cultural institutions, and the wider arts and culture sector. The programme was established to help nurture future leaders and foster greater inclusiveness within arts and culture consulting. Through project-based experience and engagement with experienced professionals, fellows can develop skills in research, planning, quantitative analysis, writing, and industry research. title: SAIIA Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme 2027: Fully Funded Research Training and Mentorship for Emerging African Researchers
summary: Applications are now open for the South African Institute of International Affairs (SAIIA) Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme 2027 , an intensive research, policy training and mentorship initiative for emerging young researchers from across Africa and the African diaspora . The programme is designed to help young postgraduate researchers strengthen the practical skills, professional networks and policy-research experience needed to move from university-based research into careers involving think tanks, public policy, international affairs, development research, academia, civil society and related fields . Selected participants will travel to Johannesburg, South Africa , for an intensive week-long training workshop scheduled for 22–26 February 2027 , with the dates currently listed as to be confirmed. The programme will cover participants’ travel to and from Johannesburg, accommodation and meals for the duration of the residency. Importantly, the programme does not end when participants leave Johannesburg. Selected researchers will receive ongoing mentorship following the residency , supporting both their professional development and the production of research outputs. SAIIA describes the Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme as a strategic capacity-building initiative that combines a youth-focused digital research platform with annual training for emerging postgraduate researchers. The programme’s broader purpose is to amplify young African voices in policy spaces and strengthen participants’ employability through research, leadership development and mentorship. SAIIA’s Youth programme states that its annual capacity-building stream brings together 20 postgraduate participants from Africa and the diaspora for intensive in-person training. SAIIA Application deadline: 30 September 2026. Training dates: 22–26 February 2027, subject to confirmation. Location: Johannesburg, South Africa. Application requirements and form: https://lnkd.in/dV2uAKQQ About the SAIIA Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme The South African Institute of International Affairs is one of Africa’s established international-affairs and policy-research institutions. Through the Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme, SAIIA is creating a structured pathway for younger researchers who want to strengthen the connection between academic research and practical policy engagement. The programme grew alongside the transformation of the former Africa Portal into the Africa Youth Portal , a platform intended to give greater visibility to research and analysis produced by emerging African voices. SAIIA describes the Africa Youth Portal as a digital hub for youth-led policy research and knowledge dissemination. Its outputs include policy briefs, web articles and blog posts, with research organized around themes including: Education Climate change Gender Peace and security Youth agency and inclusion The capacity-building component complements this publishing platform by training postgraduate researchers in the skills required to communicate research effectively to audiences beyond universities. SAIIA A Fully Funded Week-Long Research Training Programme in Johannesburg The centrepiece of the 2027 programme will be an intensive, in-person workshop in Johannesburg. Proposed training dates 22–26 February 2027 The dates are currently marked TBC , meaning applicants should remain attentive to any confirmation or schedule changes communicated by SAIIA. The residency is expected to bring together young researchers from different countries, disciplines and postgraduate levels for concentrated training, peer exchange and professional development. One of the key strengths of the initiative is that participants are not expected to finance the Johannesburg component themselves. The project will cover: Travel to Johannesburg Return travel from Johannesburg Accommodation during the programme Meals during the training period This substantially reduces the financial barriers that can prevent emerging African researchers from participating in international research-training and networking opportunities. How Many Researchers Participate? SAIIA’s programme framework states that the annual capacity-building stream trains 20 postgraduate students from across Africa and the African diaspora through a competitive selection process. The small cohort structure is intended to enable more intensive interaction among: Participants SAIIA researchers Mentors Policy professionals Other invited experts Rather than functioning as a large conference, the programme is structured around focused training and sustained professional development. From Academic Research to Policy Research One of the central purposes of the Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme is helping young researchers understand the difference between producing research mainly for academic audiences and producing research that can influence policymakers, practitioners and public debate. Previous SAIIA programme material identifies training areas such as: Differences between think-tank and academic research Writing concise and influential policy pieces Research dissemination Media engagement Digital tools for researchers Artificial intelligence tools Personal branding Career mapping The programme is therefore particularly useful for participants who may already have strong academic skills but want to learn how to communicate evidence in formats commonly used by policy institutions. Why Policy Writing Is Different From Academic Writing Many postgraduate students become familiar with long-form academic assignments, dissertations and journal-style writing. Policy organizations frequently require a different style. Researchers may need to communicate: What happened Why it matters Which stakeholders are affected What evidence supports the analysis What the implications are What policymakers should pay attention to and do so in far fewer words. The Africa Youth Portal programme is designed to help participants develop this type of concise, accessible and policy-relevant communication. Research Dissemination and Media Engagement Producing good research is only one part of becoming an effective policy researcher. Researchers also need to understand how to communicate their findings to different audiences. The programme’s emphasis on dissemination and media engagement can help participants think about how the same evidence might need to be presented differently to: Academic researchers Government officials Civil society organizations Journalists International organizations Development practitioners Young audiences The general public This ability to translate complex research into accessible formats is increasingly important for researchers seeking careers outside exclusively academic environments. AI and Digital Tools for Researchers SAIIA’s programme has also included training on AI and digital tools for researchers . SAIIA This reflects the rapidly changing research environment in which young analysts increasingly need to understand digital tools while maintaining strong standards of: Research integrity Source verification Critical analysis Responsible use of technology Independent judgment Applicants should nevertheless carefully follow the instructions in the 2027 application form regarding the use of AI in preparing application responses. Personal Branding and Career Development Academic programmes often focus heavily on research skills but provide less guidance on professional positioning. The Africa Youth Portal programme also considers how young researchers can build careers around their expertise. This can include thinking about: How to communicate research interests professionally How to develop a coherent research profile How to use LinkedIn and other professional platforms How to build a publication portfolio How to approach think tanks and policy institutions How to communicate with prospective employers How to identify longer-term career pathways This makes the programme relevant not only to future academics but also to researchers seeking careers in policy institutions, NGOs, government, international organizations and consulting. Ongoing Mentorship After the Johannesburg Residency A particularly important feature of the programme is the mentorship component. Participants will not simply attend a week of training and then leave the programme. Following the Johannesburg residency, they will receive ongoing mentorship intended to support their professional development and research outputs . SAIIA describes mentorship as an integral part of the programme and draws on its network of experienced researchers and policy professionals to support emerging researchers. This continued relationship may help participants: Refine research ideas Strengthen analytical writing Improve research outputs Navigate early research careers Understand professional policy environments Develop stronger publication strategies Opportunity to Develop Publishable Research The Africa Youth Portal is intended to provide a platform where emerging African researchers can contribute policy-focused work. SAIIA’s programme model includes opportunities for participants to produce research for publication through the Portal. The platform publishes formats such as policy briefs, web articles and blogs. For an early-career researcher, this can be particularly useful because employers frequently want evidence of actual analytical output rather than academic qualifications alone. A publication can help demonstrate an applicant’s ability to: Develop a clear research question Analyze evidence Write concisely Communicate to a non-academic audience Connect research to policy debates Who Should Apply? The programme is targeted primarily at young postgraduate researchers and emerging scholars interested in building research and policy careers. Applicants who may find the programme particularly relevant include: Honours students Master’s students PhD candidates Recent postgraduate graduates Emerging policy researchers Early-career African scholars The current call specifically emphasizes researchers from across the African continent and the diaspora . Applicants should be interested in using research to engage with public-policy, development and societal challenges affecting Africa. Age and Career Stage The programme’s established eligibility framework has targeted young researchers between 18 and 35 years old , and current information circulating with the 2027 call continues to identify this age group as the target population. The programme is intended for researchers who are still at an early stage of their academic or professional careers. Applicants should consult the current 2027 application form to confirm all final eligibility conditions before submitting. Postgraduate Study Requirements The programme is aimed at applicants who are: Currently enrolled in a postgraduate programme; or Recently completed postgraduate study. Relevant levels include: Honours Master’s PhD Current 2027 opportunity information indicates that recent graduates should generally have completed their postgraduate programme within the previous year. Applicants should provide the relevant academic documentation requested in the application form. Relevant Academic Fields The programme is multidisciplinary. Previous and current programme information identifies fields connected to areas such as: Political Science International Relations Journalism Development Studies Sociology Law Economics Foresight Studies Public Policy and related areas The central consideration is not simply the name of the degree but whether the applicant demonstrates the ability and motivation to contribute meaningful policy-oriented research on African issues. Applicants should use the current application guidance as the final authority regarding eligible disciplines. Africa and the Diaspora One important update to earlier descriptions of the programme is its explicit emphasis on both: Researchers based across the African continent and researchers from the African diaspora. SAIIA’s own Youth programme describes the annual training stream as bringing together postgraduate participants from “the continent and the diaspora.” African researchers currently studying or living outside the continent should therefore not automatically assume that being abroad makes them ineligible. The application form should be consulted for the exact citizenship or nationality documentation required. Research Themes The Africa Youth Portal organizes its research engagement around several broad themes. These include: Education Research examining educational systems, access, skills, inequality, youth transitions and the relationship between education and African development. Climate Change Work examining climate policy, adaptation, mitigation, climate justice, resilience and the social and economic consequences of environmental change. Gender Research focusing on gender equality, inclusion, representation, social norms and gendered dimensions of development and public policy. Peace and Security Research considering armed conflict, peacebuilding, security governance and related political challenges. Youth Agency and Inclusion Research examining young people not simply as beneficiaries of policy but as political, economic and social actors capable of influencing decisions affecting their communities. SAIIA identifies these themes as the core subject areas around which Africa Youth Portal outputs are organized. SAIIA Application Documents to Prepare Applicants should prepare their supporting documents before beginning the application. Current 2027 application information indicates that candidates should have the following documents available in PDF format : Curriculum Vitae Copy of ID or passport Academic transcript or proof of enrolment Recommendation letter Proposed research topic Writing sample Current application guidance also advises candidates to prepare everything before beginning because the online form may not save unfinished progress. Opportunity For Africa Curriculum Vitae Your CV should emphasize experiences relevant to research and policy. Depending on your background, these could include: Academic research Thesis or dissertation work Research assistantships Publications Policy writing Conferences Volunteer research Youth leadership Civil society involvement Internships Data analysis Journalism Advocacy International affairs activities Do not assume that lack of formal employment makes you uncompetitive. The programme is specifically designed for emerging researchers . Proposed Research Topic Applicants should think carefully about the research topic they propose. A strong topic should ideally: Address an identifiable African policy problem Be specific enough to research meaningfully Fit the Africa Youth Portal’s thematic areas Have clear contemporary relevance Be capable of producing a focused policy-oriented output A broad subject such as “climate change in Africa” is unlikely to be as effective as a clearly defined question addressing a particular country, population, institution or policy challenge. Writing Sample The writing sample is an opportunity to demonstrate how you think as a researcher. Depending on the application instructions, a suitable sample could come from: Dissertation work Academic essays Journal articles Research reports Policy briefs Published commentary Current information on the call indicates that applicants should prepare a sample demonstrating research and analytical ability. Opportunity For Africa Candidates should prioritize clarity and analytical strength rather than trying to make the writing unnecessarily complicated. Recommendation Letter Applicants should also prepare a recommendation letter. Where possible, select someone who can speak directly about your: Research ability Academic potential Reliability Analytical skills Capacity for independent work Interest in policy research An academic supervisor, lecturer or research manager who genuinely knows your work may generally provide a more useful reference than a prominent person who knows little about your research abilities. Full Participation Is Important Applicants should only apply if they are able to attend the entire Johannesburg training period. The provisional programme dates are: 22–26 February 2027 Because these dates are still marked TBC, selected applicants should remain flexible until SAIIA formally confirms the schedule. Participants should also be prepared for post-residency mentorship and research engagements , since the programme extends beyond the five-day workshop. What the Programme Covers For the Johannesburg training component, the project covers: Travel to Johannesburg Return travel Accommodation Meals Applicants should avoid assuming that unrelated personal expenses are covered unless SAIIA specifically confirms them. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the programme’s online application process. Applicants are strongly advised to prepare all required materials before opening the application form. Application requirements and form: https://lnkd.in/dV2uAKQQ Because the application may require several uploaded documents and research-related responses, candidates should not wait until the final day to start preparing. Application Deadline The deadline for the 2027 Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme is: 30 September 2026. Applicants should submit before the deadline and should not assume that incomplete applications can be corrected afterward. Key Programme Details at a Glance Programme: Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme 2027 Host: South African Institute of International Affairs Location: Johannesburg, South Africa Training dates: 22–26 February 2027, TBC Format: Week-long in-person training followed by ongoing mentorship Target group: Emerging young postgraduate researchers from Africa and the African diaspora Annual cohort: 20 postgraduate participants according to SAIIA’s programme framework SAIIA Funding: Travel to and from Johannesburg, accommodation and meals covered Major focus: Research skills, policy research, communication and professional development Research themes: Education, climate change, gender, peace and security, and youth agency and inclusion SAIIA Application deadline: 30 September 2026 Application information: https://lnkd.in/dV2uAKQQ Why the Africa Youth Portal Research Programme Matters The transition between postgraduate study and a professional research career can be difficult. A student may leave university knowing how to conduct academic research but still have little experience with: Policy briefs Think-tank writing Media engagement Professional research networks Publishing for non-academic audiences Translating research into practical policy insights The Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme is designed to address precisely this gap. SAIIA’s broader Youth programme combines policy research, policy engagement and capacity building, while the Africa Youth Portal provides a platform through which emerging African voices can contribute directly to policy discussions. SAIIA The combination of fully supported travel, intensive training, mentorship, publication-oriented research and continental networking makes the programme particularly relevant to young African researchers seeking to move from academic study toward a sustained professional research career. Conclusion The SAIIA Africa Youth Portal and Research Programme 2027 offers emerging researchers from across Africa and the African diaspora an opportunity to strengthen the practical skills needed to build careers in research and public policy. Selected participants will attend an intensive week-long workshop in Johannesburg from 22–26 February 2027, subject to confirmation , while the project covers travel, accommodation and meals . The residency is only the beginning. Participants will continue receiving mentorship following the training, helping them strengthen their research outputs and professional development. Through the wider Africa Youth Portal, SAIIA is also creating a platform for young researchers to communicate policy-relevant ideas to audiences beyond academia. The programme’s annual training stream brings together 20 postgraduate researchers and focuses on research methodologies, publishing, digital tools, personal branding and media engagement. SAIIA For postgraduate researchers who want to move from academic research toward think-tank work, policy analysis, international affairs or other evidence-based careers , the 2027 programme provides a structured opportunity to develop those skills while joining a pan-African research network.
