title: PAIE Scholars Program 2026: US$1,000 Award, Up to US$10,000 Research Support and Up to US$75,000 Pilot Funding
summary: Researchers working in low- and middle-income countries in Africa and Asia can apply for the PAIE Scholars Program , an initiative designed to help researchers develop rigorous, policy-relevant research on how artificial intelligence can be used for social good and in the fight against poverty. The program, offered through Project AI Evidence (PAIE), an initiative of the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) , combines specialized training, research concept development, assessment, potential research mentorship, proposal-development and travel support, and the possibility of substantial pilot research funding. Selected scholars will receive training in randomized evaluation and the evaluation of AI-enabled interventions. Those who successfully complete the first phase of the program will receive a US$1,000 award . Scholars who progress through the competitive subsequent stages may also receive a proposal-development and travel grant of up to US$10,000 , research mentorship, and eventually the opportunity to compete for up to US$75,000 in PAIE pilot funding . The PAIE Scholars Program therefore provides a structured pathway for researchers who want to turn an early research idea involving artificial intelligence into a rigorous evaluation capable of generating evidence relevant to policy and social outcomes. About the PAIE Scholars Program The PAIE Scholars Program supports researchers based in low- and middle-income countries in Asia and Africa who are interested in developing and leading rigorous evaluations of innovative applications of artificial intelligence for social good and poverty reduction. The program is built around the idea that AI-enabled interventions need rigorous evidence to understand whether, how, and under what circumstances they produce meaningful social or economic outcomes. Rather than requiring applicants to arrive with a fully developed research project, the program allows researchers to begin with a working concept note . Participants then refine their research ideas throughout the training, incorporating methodological knowledge and feedback from the PAIE team. The program is particularly focused on connecting research ideas involving AI with rigorous evaluation methods, including randomized evaluations. According to the program structure, successful scholars can progress through several stages, beginning with training and assessment and potentially moving toward proposal development, research mentorship, and pilot funding. However, advancement from one stage to another is competitive, and selection for the initial cohort does not automatically guarantee subsequent support or funding. What Does the PAIE Scholars Program Offer? The program provides several forms of support at different stages. 1. Specialized Research Training Selected scholars will participate in structured training covering: Randomized evaluation methods. Evaluation of AI-enabled interventions. Research design and evidence generation. Materials related to AI evaluation. Relevant methodological readings and learning resources. Live online workshops. A PAIE-administered assessment. The training includes selected modules from J-PAL 102x: Designing and Running Randomized Evaluations , which forms part of the MITx MicroMasters in Data, Economics, and Design of Policy. Participants will also engage with the AI Evidence Playbook , the AI Evaluation Playbook , and related reading materials. The program will include live online workshops focused specifically on evaluating AI-enabled interventions. 2. US$1,000 Award Scholars who successfully complete the first phase of the program will receive a US$1,000 award . The award is conditional on meeting the requirements of the first phase. Specifically, scholars must complete their assigned training requirements, pass the PAIE-administered assessment, and submit a revised concept note that meets the program requirements. The US$1,000 award is separate from any later proposal-development and travel support. Importantly, receiving this award does not automatically guarantee research mentorship, pilot funding, or advancement to subsequent stages. 3. Concept Note Development Applicants will enter the program with a working concept note submitted during the application process. The concept note does not have to represent a fully developed research project. Applicants also do not need to have an implementing partner at the initial application stage. During the training, scholars will refine their concept notes using what they learn from the program. The revised concept note will form the basis for consideration for proposal-development and travel support and potential research mentorship. The revised concept note is expected to address areas such as: The policy or social problem motivating the proposed research. The AI-enabled intervention or policy application being considered. The research question. Why rigorous evidence is necessary. The relevant population and research setting. The scholar s initial evaluation design. Potential outcomes and data sources. A potential implementing partner, if one has been identified. An initial strategy for identifying an implementing partner if one has not yet been identified. The pathway toward a randomized evaluation. What a potential pilot study would establish. Further research-development needs. How proposal-development and travel support would be used. 4. Proposal-Development and Travel Grant of Up to US$10,000 Scholars selected for the next stage may receive a proposal-development and travel grant of up to US$10,000 . This support is designed to help researchers transform their preliminary research ideas into full pilot proposals. The grant can support activities such as: Conducting background research. Identifying or developing relationships with potential implementing partners. Visiting potential field research sites. Assessing the availability and suitability of existing administrative or survey data. Conducting preliminary analysis of existing data where such analysis does not constitute human-subjects research. Refining the research question. Improving the evaluation design. Preparing a pilot proposal. Developing the research budget. However, the proposal-development and travel grant cannot be used to conduct human-subjects research or collect data from research participants . 5. Potential Research Mentorship Researchers who receive proposal-development support may also receive research mentorship, depending on their needs and the availability of appropriate mentors. Mentors may include J-PAL-affiliated professors or invited researchers with relevant methodological or subject-matter expertise. Mentorship may cover areas such as: Refining the research question. Developing the evaluation design. Establishing or strengthening implementing partnerships. Preparing for fieldwork. Developing the pilot proposal. Strengthening the overall research strategy. PAIE staff and the J-PAL research team may also provide additional support during the proposal-development process. However, receiving research mentorship or a proposal-development and travel grant does not guarantee subsequent pilot funding. PAIE Pilot Funding of Up to US$75,000 One of the later stages of the program provides an opportunity for eligible scholars to submit a full proposal for an early-stage pilot study. Scholars may reach this stage after completing the proposal-development process or, where a project is already sufficiently developed, they may be invited to proceed directly to a full pilot proposal. The pilot research should have a clear research question and be designed to develop into, or inform, a future full-scale randomized evaluation. Successful pilot research could be used to: Test the feasibility of an AI-enabled intervention. Test aspects of the proposed research design. Refine measurement strategies. Develop implementation and research logistics. Collect pilot data. Facilitate access to administrative data. Generate information needed to design a larger randomized evaluation. Build evidence that could potentially inform policy at scale. By the pilot-proposal stage, researchers are expected to have an implementing partner and a sufficiently developed research design. Pilot proposals will undergo a separate competitive review. Successful proposals may receive up to US$75,000 in PAIE pilot funding . Being invited to submit a pilot proposal does not guarantee that funding will ultimately be awarded. Who Is Eligible for the PAIE Scholars Program? The PAIE Scholars Program is specifically designed for resident scholars based in low- and middle-income countries in Asia and Africa , according to the World Bank s classification. For this program, a resident scholar is a researcher who: Has completed a PhD. Has a primary professional affiliation with a university located in an eligible country. May hold additional positions at other organizations, provided that the primary university affiliation is in an eligible country. Applicants should therefore carefully check the program s definitive list of eligible countries before applying. Academic and Research Requirements Applicants must satisfy several academic and professional requirements. Completed PhD Applicants must have completed a PhD in economics or another relevant empirical discipline . Advanced Quantitative Training Applicants must have advanced training in quantitative methods. Relevant areas include: Statistics. Econometrics. Causal inference. Experimental methods. Machine learning. This quantitative foundation is important because the program focuses heavily on rigorous evaluation and evidence generation. Interest in AI Evaluation Applicants must demonstrate an interest in evaluating how AI-enabled interventions affect social or economic outcomes . The proposed research should therefore connect artificial intelligence with a meaningful social, economic, development, or policy question that can be investigated through rigorous empirical research. English Proficiency Applicants must have sufficient English proficiency to: Complete the required coursework. Participate in the training. Complete the assessment. Prepare research outputs in English. Availability Applicants must be willing and available to complete all required components of the program. The initial training is tentatively expected to run for approximately three months, from November 2026 through January 2027 . Selected scholars should expect to dedicate approximately four to ten hours per week , depending on their previous training and familiarity with randomized evaluations. The final schedule, coursework, and expected time commitment will be communicated before the program begins. Do Applicants Need a Fully Developed Research Project? No. One of the important features of the PAIE Scholars Program is that applicants do not need to have a fully developed research project at the time of application . Applicants submit a working concept note describing the research idea they would like to develop. The concept note does not need to contain a complete intervention or evaluation design. Applicants are also not required to have an implementing partner at the initial application stage . This allows eligible researchers to enter the program with an early-stage idea and use the training and support provided by PAIE to strengthen that idea. Applicants also do not need to have an existing relationship with a J-PAL-affiliated professor or invited researcher in order to apply. What Documents Are Required? The application requires applicants to provide information about their academic background, research experience, quantitative training, and interest in evaluating AI-enabled interventions. Applicants will be asked to submit: A curriculum vitae (CV). One to three examples of their research. Brief statements describing: Their research experience. Their experience with randomized evaluations. Their interest in evaluating AI-enabled interventions. Their interest in participating in the PAIE Scholars Program. A working concept note describing the research idea they would like to develop and explaining how the idea could ultimately lead to a randomized evaluation. The application form provides the complete requirements and applicable word limits. How the PAIE Scholars Program Works The program follows a staged process rather than providing all forms of support immediately. Stage 1: Application Researchers submit an online application containing their academic and research information, supporting materials, statements, and working concept note. Stage 2: Selection A cohort of scholars is selected to participate in the initial program. Selection into this cohort does not guarantee progression to later stages. Stage 3: Training Selected scholars participate in training covering randomized evaluations and the evaluation of AI-enabled interventions. Stage 4: Assessment Participants complete a PAIE-administered proctored assessment based on the training. The PAIE assessment is a requirement of the program. It is important to distinguish this assessment from the official MITx assessment. The PAIE-administered assessment is separate and does not result in an MITx certificate. Scholars may later complete the official MITx assessment and potentially earn an MITx certificate, subject to the applicable MITx requirements and assessment schedule. Researchers who already have sufficient training in randomized evaluation may complete selected 102x modules. Stage 5: Revised Concept Note Scholars who complete their assigned training requirements and pass the PAIE assessment will submit a revised concept note. The revised concept note becomes the basis for consideration for proposal-development and travel support and potential research mentorship. Stage 6: Proposal Development and Mentorship PAIE will review the revised concept notes and select a subset of scholars for proposal-development and travel support. Depending on their needs and mentor availability, selected scholars may also receive research mentorship. Stage 7: Full Pilot Proposal Scholars who successfully develop their research ideas may proceed to the full pilot-proposal stage. Researchers invited to submit a pilot proposal will need to have a sufficiently developed research design and, at this stage, an implementing partner. Stage 8: Competitive Pilot Funding Review Full pilot proposals undergo a separate competitive review. Successful proposals may receive up to US$75,000 in PAIE pilot funding . Application Deadline The PAIE Scholars Program 2026 application deadline is October 16, 2026, at 12:00 PM Eastern Time (ET) . Applications opened on September 17, 2026 . Prospective applicants should prepare their materials well in advance of the deadline because the application requires a CV, research examples, multiple statements, and a working concept note. PAIE Scholars Program Timeline The current program timeline is as follows: Activity Timeline Applications open September 17, 2026 Application deadline October 16, 2026 at 12 PM ET Scholars selected Early November 2026 Training begins November 2026 Initial training period Approximately November 2026–January 2027 PAIE-administered assessment To be confirmed Revised concept notes due To be confirmed Proposal-development grant decisions To be confirmed Pilot-proposal timeline To be announced Additional dates, including the pilot-proposal timeline, will be communicated to selected scholars. Key Points Applicants Should Understand Prospective applicants should pay attention to several important aspects of the program. First, the program is designed specifically for researchers based in eligible low- and middle-income countries in Africa and Asia . Second, applicants must have completed a PhD in economics or another relevant empirical discipline and possess advanced quantitative training. Third, applicants do not need to arrive with a complete research project. A working concept note is sufficient at the application stage. Fourth, an implementing partner is not required when initially applying. However, an implementing partner is expected by the pilot-proposal stage. Fifth, the initial US$1,000 award is conditional on successful completion of the first phase and should not be interpreted as guaranteed funding for subsequent research. Sixth, proposal-development and travel support of up to US$10,000 is available only to scholars selected for that stage. Finally, pilot funding of up to US$75,000 is subject to a separate competitive review. Participation in earlier stages does not guarantee pilot funding. Why the Working Concept Note Matters The working concept note is an important part of the PAIE Scholars Program because it provides the starting point for the research-development process. Applicants are not expected to have finalized every aspect of their research methodology. Instead, they should clearly communicate the research problem they want to investigate, the potential role of an AI-enabled intervention, the population and setting they are interested in, and how the idea could eventually be evaluated rigorously. During the program, scholars will have an opportunity to improve their concept notes using the methods and knowledge gained through the training. The revised concept note can then serve as the basis for consideration for further proposal-development support and research mentorship. What Kind of Research Is the Program Looking For? The program focuses on research involving innovative applications of artificial intelligence for social good and in the fight against poverty . Applicants should therefore consider research questions that examine how AI-enabled interventions may affect social or economic outcomes and how these effects can be evaluated using rigorous empirical methods. The program s emphasis on randomized evaluation means that applicants should think about how their initial research idea could eventually develop into a rigorous evaluation capable of producing credible evidence. The concept note should therefore not simply describe an AI technology. It should begin to establish a meaningful research question and a pathway toward evaluating the intervention. About Project AI Evidence and J-PAL The PAIE Scholars Program is part of Project AI Evidence (PAIE) . Project AI Evidence focuses on identifying, evaluating, and scaling innovative applications of artificial intelligence for social good and poverty reduction. It brings together AI adopters, technology companies, and researchers to strengthen evidence around AI applications. PAIE is an initiative of the Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab (J-PAL) . J-PAL s work includes research and initiatives focused on generating evidence and using that evidence to inform policy. How to Apply Interested applicants should complete the official online application before the stated deadline. The application requires information concerning the applicant s academic background, research experience, quantitative training, and interest in evaluating AI-enabled interventions. Applicants should prepare the required materials, including: CV. One to three research examples. Research experience statement. Randomized-evaluation experience statement. Statement of interest in evaluating AI-enabled interventions. Statement explaining interest in the PAIE Scholars Program. Working concept note. Applicants should also carefully review the official eligibility requirements and the definitive list of eligible countries before submitting an application. Application deadline: October 16, 2026, at 12:00 PM ET. CLICK HERE TO APPLY Contact Information Applicants with questions about the PAIE Scholars Program can contact the PAIE team by email at paie@povertyactionlab.org . Click HERE for more information about the PAIE Scholars Program 2026. Conclusion The PAIE Scholars Program 2026 provides a structured research-development opportunity for eligible researchers in low- and middle-income countries in Africa and Asia who are interested in studying the social and economic effects of AI-enabled interventions. The program goes beyond conventional research training by combining methodological instruction with concept-note development, assessment, potential research mentorship, proposal-development and travel support, and the possibility of substantial pilot research funding. Selected scholars can receive a US$1,000 award after successfully completing the first phase. Those who progress through the subsequent competitive stage may receive up to US$10,000 in proposal-development and travel support , while successful pilot proposals may ultimately receive up to US$75,000 in PAIE pilot funding . Because later stages are competitive, applicants should understand that participation in the initial training does not automatically lead to mentorship, proposal-development funding, or pilot funding. For eligible researchers with a PhD, strong quantitative-methods training, and a research interest in evaluating AI-enabled interventions, the program offers a pathway for developing an early research idea into a more rigorous evaluation proposal. Interested applicants should review the eligibility requirements, prepare the required application materials, develop a clear working concept note, and submit the application before the October 16, 2026 deadline at 12:00 PM ET . title: Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program (Trailblazers 5.0): Applications Open for Recent Graduates
summary: Applications are open for the Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program (Trailblazers 5.0) , an early-career development opportunity designed for ambitious recent graduates who are ready to accelerate their professional growth within a global organisation. Based in Lagos-Island, Lagos, Nigeria , the programme provides successful candidates with practical exposure to Reckitt’s business through rotations across its Commercial and Supply functions . Participants will gain experience with end-to-end business processes, contribute to real business projects from the beginning of their journey, and receive mentorship from experienced business leaders. The programme is designed to develop the next generation of Reckitt leaders , making it particularly relevant to graduates who want more than a conventional entry-level role and are interested in gaining broad, cross-functional business experience early in their careers. About Reckitt Reckitt is a global company behind a portfolio of well-known brands across the health, hygiene and nutrition sectors. The company describes its purpose around protecting, healing and nurturing in pursuit of a cleaner and healthier world, with its products and brands serving consumers across international markets. For graduates and students specifically, Reckitt offers internships, apprenticeships and graduate programmes across different locations worldwide. Its graduate programmes are designed to provide participants with practical experiences, learning opportunities and responsibility for projects involving global brands. In Nigeria, Reckitt Benckiser (Nigeria) Ltd has an office at Heritage Place, 21 Lugard Avenue, Ikoyi, Lagos. About the Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program The Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program, also known as Trailblazers 5.0 , provides young graduates with an accelerated pathway for developing their careers within a global organisation. Rather than placing participants exclusively within one narrow area of the business, the programme provides exposure to end-to-end business processes through rotations across Commercial and Supply functions . This rotational structure gives trainees the opportunity to understand how different parts of an international consumer goods business connect and operate. Most importantly, trainees are expected to work on genuine business projects and engage with real-life business scenarios from the beginning of the programme. This practical approach is intended to help participants move beyond theoretical knowledge gained at university and begin developing the commercial awareness, problem-solving capabilities and professional judgement needed in a corporate environment. The programme ultimately aims to identify and develop people who could become the next generation of leaders within Reckitt. Reckitt Nigeria Trailblazers 5.0 Program Overview Key details of the opportunity include: Programme: Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program Programme name: Trailblazers 5.0 Company: Reckitt Location: Lagos-Island, Lagos, Nigeria Target group: Recent graduates Eligible degree disciplines: Any degree Graduation years: 2022 to 2025 Minimum academic requirement: Upper Second Class Honours NYSC requirement: Applicants must have completed NYSC by December 2026 Rotational areas: Commercial and Supply functions Requisition ID: 86550 Date posted: 19 September 2026 The vacancy is currently listed on Reckitt’s official graduate careers platform. What Successful Trailblazers Will Experience The Reckitt Nigeria Management Trainee Program is structured to combine professional development with hands-on business exposure. Successful candidates can expect several important elements during their experience. 1. Cross-Functional Business Rotations Participants will gain experience through rotations across Reckitt’s Commercial and Supply functions . Rotational programmes can provide early-career professionals with a broader understanding of how different departments contribute to the overall organisation. Instead of learning about only one business function, Reckitt Trailblazers will have the opportunity to gain exposure to different parts of the company s operations and understand the connections between them. 2. Exposure to End-to-End Business Processes Reckitt specifically highlights exposure to end-to-end business processes as an important component of the programme. This means participants can gain a broader perspective on how activities across different business functions contribute to Reckitt’s operations. For a recent graduate, such exposure can be valuable in building commercial awareness and understanding how decisions made in one part of a business may influence another. 3. Work on Real Business Projects Trailblazers will not simply observe experienced employees at work. Reckitt states that participants will have opportunities to work on business projects and real-life business scenarios from Day One . This gives successful applicants an opportunity to begin applying their academic knowledge, analytical capabilities, communication skills and problem-solving abilities in a professional environment. 4. Work With Major Consumer Brands Successful applicants will have the opportunity to build their careers while working within the organisation behind some of the world s recognised health, hygiene and nutrition brands. Reckitt describes itself as a global organisation focused on delivering better health to more people through its portfolio and operations. 5. Mentorship From Business Leaders Another significant element of the Trailblazers 5.0 programme is mentorship. Reckitt states that participants will have opportunities to be mentored by its business leaders. For recent graduates transitioning from university into a corporate environment, access to experienced professionals can provide valuable guidance while they develop their understanding of business operations, workplace expectations and leadership. Who Can Apply for the Reckitt Nigeria Management Trainee Program? Reckitt has outlined specific eligibility requirements for candidates interested in becoming part of Trailblazers 5.0. Applicants should carefully review these requirements before submitting an application. Recent Graduate Requirement Applicants must be recent graduates who completed their studies between 2022 and 2025 . This makes the programme particularly suitable for individuals who are in the early stages of their professional careers. Degree Requirement Reckitt states that it is open to graduates from any degree discipline . Therefore, applicants are not restricted to a specific academic subject such as business, marketing, engineering or supply chain. This broad degree eligibility opens the opportunity to graduates from a variety of academic backgrounds, provided they satisfy the other programme requirements. Academic Classification Applicants must have graduated with at least an Upper Second Class Honours degree . Candidates should therefore ensure that their academic qualification satisfies this requirement before applying. NYSC Requirement Candidates must have completed the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) programme by December 2026 . This is a particularly important eligibility requirement for applicants to note. Candidates who have already completed NYSC or will complete it by the specified December 2026 timeframe can consider applying, provided they meet the programme s other requirements. What Kind of Candidate Is Reckitt Looking For? Academic qualifications alone are not the only consideration. Reckitt describes its ideal Nigeria Trailblazer as someone who is: Curious Driven Ambitious These qualities align with the nature of a management trainee programme where participants are expected to learn quickly, adapt to different business environments and contribute to practical projects. Reckitt also states that it considers potential alongside experience and encourages candidates who believe the organisation and role are a good fit to consider applying even if they do not feel they meet every point in the job description. Skills Needed to Succeed in Trailblazers 5.0 Reckitt identifies several capabilities as important for success in the programme. Ownership Participants should be prepared to take responsibility for their work and contribution. Working on genuine business projects from the beginning means trainees may need to demonstrate accountability and a willingness to take initiative. Self-Awareness The ability to understand personal strengths, development areas and behaviour can be particularly important in a rotational environment where participants may encounter different teams, responsibilities and working styles. Mental Agility Participants should be capable of adapting their thinking as they encounter new situations and business challenges. This may be especially relevant when moving between different functions during the programme. Proactiveness Rather than waiting to be directed at every stage, successful trainees are expected to demonstrate initiative and an active approach to learning and contributing. Communication Skills Effective communication is important when collaborating with colleagues, managers and stakeholders across different parts of an organisation. Attention to Detail Candidates should be capable of maintaining accuracy and carefully considering details while working on business assignments and projects. Analytical Skills The ability to examine information, identify patterns and draw useful conclusions can help trainees approach business challenges more effectively. Problem-Solving Skills As participants will encounter real business scenarios, they should be comfortable identifying problems, considering possible solutions and contributing to practical outcomes. Together, Reckitt lists ownership, self-awareness, mental agility, proactiveness, communication, attention to detail, analytical ability and problem-solving among the skills associated with success in the role. Why Consider a Graduate Programme at Reckitt? Reckitt describes its graduate programmes more broadly as opportunities that allow participants to develop quickly through a range of experiences and learning opportunities. Graduates can be trusted with responsibility and opportunities to work on projects associated with global brands while developing their careers within the organisation. For participants in Nigeria s Trailblazers 5.0 programme specifically, the combination of Commercial and Supply rotations, practical projects, real-world business scenarios and mentorship creates a development-focused early-career experience. Employee Benefits and Support at Reckitt Beyond professional development, Reckitt highlights a broader employee support framework. The company states that inclusion is an important part of its workplace approach and that it works alongside four global Employee Resource Groups to support employees throughout their careers. Benefits and support highlighted by Reckitt include: Parental benefits Employee Assistance Program Life insurance for employees globally Additional benefits according to the applicable local market Global share plans Short-term incentives for eligible positions Career support and development The precise benefits available to an individual employee may depend on the role, eligibility requirements, location and applicable company policies. Reckitt also states that its reward approach follows a pay-for-performance philosophy. Reckitt s Approach to Inclusion and Equal Opportunity Reckitt states that qualified applicants are considered for employment without discrimination based on protected characteristics. The company also acknowledges that strong candidates may not always meet every single point in a job description and states that it hires for potential as well as experience . This approach is especially relevant in an early-career programme where applicants may have limited professional experience but demonstrate strong potential, ambition and transferable capabilities. How to Apply for the Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program Interested candidates should submit their applications through Reckitt s official careers platform . Applicants can follow these general steps: Visit the official Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program vacancy. Review the complete programme description and eligibility requirements. Select the application option on the vacancy page. Sign in or create the required candidate profile if prompted. Complete all requested personal, educational and professional information accurately. Upload any requested supporting documents. Review the application carefully before submission. Submit the application through Reckitt s recruitment system. Applicants should ensure that their application information accurately demonstrates how they satisfy the academic, graduation-year and NYSC requirements. Official application page: Apply for the Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program Application Deadline The official Reckitt vacancy reviewed for this article does not currently state a specific application deadline. Some third-party opportunity and recruitment websites list 10 October 2026 as the closing date. However, because this date is not currently displayed on Reckitt s official vacancy page, applicants should not rely exclusively on the third-party deadline. Interested candidates are therefore strongly encouraged to apply as early as possible while the official vacancy remains open and monitor the Reckitt careers page for any changes to the recruitment timeline. Important Information for Applicants Before submitting an application, candidates should pay particular attention to the following: The opportunity is specifically advertised as the Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program (Trailblazers 5.0) . The advertised location is Lagos-Island, Lagos, Nigeria . Applicants can come from any degree discipline . Candidates must have graduated between 2022 and 2025 . A minimum Upper Second Class Honours degree is required. Candidates must have completed NYSC by December 2026 . Reckitt is looking for candidates who demonstrate curiosity, ambition and drive. Applicants should demonstrate skills including communication, analytical thinking, problem-solving, ownership, proactiveness and attention to detail. Applications should be submitted through the official Reckitt careers platform. APPLY NOW Conclusion The Reckitt Nigeria 2026 Management Trainee Program (Trailblazers 5.0) presents an early-career opportunity for recent graduates seeking practical exposure within a global health, hygiene and nutrition business. Through rotations across Commercial and Supply functions , participants will have an opportunity to develop an understanding of end-to-end business processes while contributing to real projects and business scenarios from the beginning of their journey. The combination of cross-functional exposure, practical responsibilities and mentorship from experienced business leaders makes the programme particularly relevant to ambitious graduates who want to develop their commercial, analytical, communication, problem-solving and leadership capabilities. Candidates who graduated between 2022 and 2025 , hold at least an Upper Second Class Honours degree , and will have completed NYSC by December 2026 should review the complete requirements and consider submitting an application while the official vacancy remains available. Applicants should use Reckitt s official recruitment platform for the latest programme information and application instructions. Visit the OFY website for more Job Opportunities . title: HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program 2027 in Germany: Research Fellowship for International Scholars
summary: Applications are now open for the HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program 2027 in Hamburg, Germany , offering accomplished researchers and scholars an opportunity to pursue independent research in the fields of peace, security, political violence, European security, emerging technologies, climate security, and related interdisciplinary areas. Jointly offered by the Hamburg Institute for Advanced Study (HIAS) and the Institute for Peace Research and Security Policy at the University of Hamburg (IFSH) , the fellowship provides selected scholars with the opportunity to live and work in Hamburg while advancing an independent research project within an interdisciplinary and internationally connected academic environment. The fellowship is designed primarily for outstanding scholars who have completed a doctorate and demonstrated substantial academic achievement. However, applications from artists, policymakers, and other professionals may also be considered when their work is closely connected to the fellowship s research priorities and engages substantively with scholarly inquiry. Selected fellows will benefit from financial support, a fully equipped workspace, interdisciplinary academic exchange, connections to Hamburg s research community, an IFSH academic tandem partner, and support with accommodation and family arrangements. The application deadline is November 16, 2026 , and the earliest possible fellowship start date is October 2027 . About the HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program The Joint Fellowship Program brings together the resources and intellectual communities of HIAS and IFSH to provide researchers with an environment where they can develop innovative ideas and pursue ambitious research projects. IFSH is a Hamburg-based research institution specialising in peace and security studies. Through the fellowship, researchers can work within an environment focused on contemporary questions surrounding peace, conflict, security, resilience, political violence, international relations, technology, and societal change. At the same time, fellows become part of the interdisciplinary community at HIAS, where internationally renowned researchers and professionals from a wide range of academic backgrounds come together. The program is particularly interested in applicants who demonstrate: Significant academic achievements; Intellectual curiosity; An interdisciplinary and international research profile; Strong interest in interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary exchange; Willingness to cooperate with researchers at IFSH and fellows at HIAS; and Interest in communicating their research beyond specialised academic audiences. Applicants are also encouraged to consider how their proposed projects could contribute to broader public understanding of their research topic. Research Areas for the 2027 Fellowship The HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program particularly welcomes research projects addressing, or closely connected to, several major areas of peace and security research. 1. Societal Perspectives on Peace and Security Researchers working on the relationship between societies, political systems, violence, radicalisation, and security are encouraged to apply. Relevant subjects include: Societal perspectives on peace and security; Political violence; Fascism; Political and societal polarisation; Radicalisation; Counterterrorism; and Related social and political developments affecting peace and security. Projects that investigate these issues through innovative or interdisciplinary approaches are particularly encouraged. 2. Great Power Conflict, Arms Dynamics and Emerging Technologies The fellowship also welcomes researchers examining international strategic competition and the changing technological dimensions of security. Relevant areas include: Great power conflict; Arms dynamics; Deterrence; Strategic stability; Emerging technologies; Cybersecurity; and Related developments affecting international peace and security. Researchers may explore how technological transformation influences military strategy, international competition, deterrence relationships, institutional responses, and the wider international security environment. 3. European Security and Regional Security Architecture European security is another major area of interest. Relevant research topics include: European security architecture; European regional security organisations; The future of European security; and Broader questions concerning institutions, cooperation, conflict, and security arrangements within Europe. Projects may examine existing security structures as well as emerging challenges and possible transformations in European security. 4. Climate Change, Crisis Resilience and Civil Protection The fellowship additionally encourages projects examining the relationship between environmental change, crises, resilience, and security. Relevant subjects include: Climate change and security; Polycrisis; Disaster response; Disaster preparedness; Crisis resilience; Civil protection; and Related interdisciplinary approaches to contemporary security challenges. Projects that connect these subjects with perspectives from different academic disciplines are especially welcome. Interdisciplinary Research Is Strongly Encouraged A major characteristic of the HIAS and IFSH fellowship is its emphasis on interdisciplinary and transdisciplinary research. Applicants are therefore encouraged to propose projects that benefit from interaction across different fields of study. The selection process considers whether a project: Opens up new research questions or ways of thinking; Benefits from engagement with other disciplines; Addresses issues relevant to the fellowship s core research areas; Is suitable for an Institute for Advanced Study environment; Can be connected with an appropriate academic tandem partner at IFSH; and Can realistically be undertaken within the research environment available through HIAS, IFSH, and Hamburg. Who Can Apply for the HIAS and IFSH Fellowship? The program is primarily intended for accomplished scholars with strong academic records. For applicants working in academia, a doctorate is mandatory . The minimum academic requirement is a doctorate in one of the following broad areas: Humanities; Social sciences; Natural sciences; or Life sciences. Candidates should demonstrate an academic and research profile relevant to the fellowship. Selection criteria include: A completed doctorate; Publications in relevant academic journals or comparable publication outlets; An interdisciplinary and international research profile; Relevant research experience connected with the fellowship s core research areas; Prestigious prizes and awards, where applicable; and A very good command of English. The fellowship takes applicants career stages into consideration and places particular emphasis on the future potential of early-career researchers . Opportunities for Artists, Policymakers and Other Professionals Although the program is strongly research-oriented, eligibility is not necessarily limited to conventional academic career paths. Applications from artists, policymakers, and other professionals may also be considered. Their work must, however: Be closely connected to the fellowship s research focus; and Engage substantively with scholarly inquiry. This allows the fellowship to incorporate perspectives beyond traditional academia while maintaining a strong connection to rigorous intellectual and research-based work. Commitment to Equal Opportunities and Diversity HIAS and IFSH are committed to equal opportunities and actively encourage applications from groups that may be underrepresented within research and academia. The fellowship particularly welcomes applications from: Female scholars; Non-binary scholars; Early-career researchers; and Individuals from regions that are usually underrepresented in research and academia. The fellowship also considers diversity when forming the broader group of scholars at IFSH and each cohort of fellows at HIAS. Factors considered include diversity in: Academic disciplines; Countries of origin; Gender; and Career stages. Applicants From the Hamburg Metropolitan Region Are Not Eligible The fellowship is intended to bring scholars and professionals into the Hamburg research environment. For this reason, applicants from within the metropolitan region of Hamburg are not eligible . Fellows are expected to live and work in Hamburg for the duration of their fellowship. Consequently, proposed projects must be suitable for being undertaken on-site at HIAS and IFSH . Applicants seeking a fully remote fellowship arrangement should therefore note that the program requires physical presence in Hamburg. Fellowship Duration and Dates The HIAS and IFSH academic year generally runs from: October 1 to June 30 of the following year. The earliest possible starting date is October 2027 . Applicants must indicate their preferred fellowship period when submitting their application. The proposed stay must last: A minimum of three months ; and A maximum of nine months . Applicants should also note that: July, August, and September are not fellowship months. Candidates should take these restrictions into account when proposing their preferred period of residence. Financial Support The fellowship is funded by IFSH. Funding can be provided through either: A stipend paid to the fellow; or Reimbursement of the fellow s home institution for the cost of a teaching replacement. Applicants are also encouraged to explore whether their home institutions can provide financial support during the fellowship. This could include arrangements such as: A sabbatical; Paid research leave; or Other forms of institutional financial contribution. Any possible financial contribution from an applicant s home institution is highly encouraged and should be mentioned in the application. Independent Research and Academic Freedom One of the principal advantages of the fellowship is the freedom given to fellows to pursue their own research. Selected fellows can work independently on their proposed projects while benefiting from interdisciplinary intellectual exchange within the communities of HIAS and IFSH. This structure provides researchers with time and space to concentrate on their projects while remaining connected to scholars from other disciplines and research traditions. Fully Equipped Workspace in Hamburg Fellows receive access to a fully equipped workspace in central Hamburg . They also benefit from ongoing support from the HIAS and IFSH teams throughout their stay. The working environment is intended to provide fellows with the practical resources and institutional support necessary to focus on their research and participate fully in the fellowship community. IFSH Academic Tandem Partner Every fellow is expected to collaborate with an academic tandem partner based at IFSH. The tandem structure is an important component of the fellowship. Through their IFSH tandem partner, fellows can gain access to: Relevant local academic networks; Research infrastructure; Institutional expertise; Potential collaborators; and Knowledge of Hamburg s wider research environment. Applicants are asked to identify possible academic tandem partners from IFSH in their application. However, applicants do not need to have established contact with the potential tandem partner before applying . Simply naming an appropriate potential tandem partner is sufficient. A letter of intent is requested only when the applicant and prospective tandem partner already know each other and intend to collaborate. Access to HIAS Member Institutions In addition to the collaboration available through IFSH, HIAS will assist fellows in identifying and connecting with potential cooperation partners at one of its ten member institutions . This provides fellows with opportunities to broaden their research networks and identify relevant scholars, expertise, or resources within Hamburg s wider academic community. Academic Program and Mandatory Participation The fellowship involves more than independent research. Fellows are expected to participate actively in the academic life of HIAS. Mandatory activities include: Weekly lunches; and Colloquia and dinners at HIAS. Fellows may also participate in additional excursions organised as part of the program. Active participation in the academic program is mandatory, reflecting the fellowship s emphasis on intellectual exchange and community building. Family-Friendly Fellowship in Hamburg HIAS and IFSH recognise that researchers may relocate with their families during longer research stays. Selected fellows may therefore have access to accommodation in the centrally located guesthouse of the University of Hamburg . The guesthouse provides fully furnished apartments equipped with cooking facilities. The institutions also welcome fellows accompanied by: Life partners; and Children. HIAS and IFSH can provide assistance with finding: Suitable accommodation; Schools; and Day care facilities. This family-friendly approach can help researchers planning a stay of several months in Hamburg. How Applications Will Be Evaluated Applications are evaluated both on the applicant s profile and the quality and suitability of the proposed research project. Applicant Evaluation Criteria Selection considers: A doctorate in the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, or life sciences; Publications in relevant academic journals or comparable publication outlets; Evidence of an interdisciplinary and international research profile; Research experience related to the fellowship s core research areas; Prestigious prizes and awards, where relevant; and A very good command of English. Career stage will also be considered, with particular attention given to the future potential of early-career researchers. Project Evaluation Criteria Reviewers will consider whether the proposed project: Opens up new questions and ways of thinking; Benefits from interaction with other academic disciplines; Addresses questions connected to the fellowship s core research topics; Is suitable for an Institute for Advanced Study environment; Can be matched with an appropriate IFSH tandem partner; and Is feasible within the research environments of HIAS, IFSH, and Hamburg. Applicants should therefore make a clear case not only for the quality of their research idea but also for why Hamburg, HIAS, and IFSH are appropriate environments for undertaking the project. Application Requirements Applications must be submitted in English . All required documents should be combined and uploaded as one PDF file through the official application form. Applicants should prepare the following materials carefully. 1. Cover Letter The cover letter should state: The applicant s desired fellowship period; Possible academic tandem partner or partners at IFSH; Any possible partial financing through a sabbatical, paid leave, or similar arrangement, where applicable; and How the applicant s research profile would enrich the fellowship group, IFSH, and the wider Hamburg research environment. The cover letter provides candidates with an opportunity to explain why they are particularly well suited to the fellowship and how their participation could contribute to the broader intellectual community. 2. Letter of Intent From a Prospective Tandem Partner Applicants may include a one-page letter of intent from their prospective IFSH tandem partner where applicable. Importantly, this document is not mandatory for every applicant. A letter of intent is requested only where the applicant and prospective tandem partner: Are already acquainted; and Intend to collaborate. Applicants who have not previously contacted an IFSH researcher can simply name a possible tandem partner in their application. Prior contact is therefore not required . 3. List of Most Important Publications Applicants should provide a list of their most important publications. The publication list must not exceed two pages . Candidates should use this section to demonstrate the relevance and strength of their research record. 4. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must submit a CV. The CV should include relevant professional and academic information as well as details of: Prizes; and Awards. Applicants should ensure that the CV clearly demonstrates their academic trajectory, relevant research experience, and interdisciplinary or international experience. 5. Research Project Description Applicants must provide a description of their planned fellowship project. The project description must not exceed three pages . Given the evaluation criteria, applicants should clearly explain: The research problem or question; The project s relevance; Its innovative contribution; Its relationship to the fellowship s research priorities; Its interdisciplinary dimensions; Why interaction with other disciplines would benefit the project; Why HIAS and IFSH provide an appropriate research environment; and How the project can realistically be completed or substantially advanced during the proposed fellowship period. 6. Project Description for a Non-Specialist Audience Applicants must also submit a separate description of their project aimed at a non-specialist audience . This document must not exceed one page . This requirement reflects the fellowship s interest in projects that can contribute to broader public understanding. Applicants should therefore communicate the significance and objectives of their research in clear and accessible language. 7. Optional Online Video, Talk or Lecture Applicants may additionally provide a link to an online: Video; Talk; or Lecture. This component is optional. Application Deadline The deadline to submit an application for the HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program is: November 16, 2026 Applications must be uploaded in English as a single PDF file through the official application form by the deadline. Prospective applicants should allow sufficient time to prepare their research proposal, publication list, CV, cover letter, and non-specialist project description. Data Processing Applicants should be aware that submitting an application constitutes consent to the purpose-related processing of their personal data. Application information will be shared with: HIAS committees; IFSH committees; and External reviewers where necessary. Applicants should take this into account when submitting their application materials. Application Enquiries Applicants with questions regarding the application procedure or required documents may contact: Dr. Kerstin Bischl Email: bischl@ifsh.de Candidates are encouraged to carefully review the requirements and prepare all required documents before submitting their application. APPLY NOW Why Consider the HIAS and IFSH Joint Fellowship Program? The fellowship offers researchers the opportunity to combine independent scholarship with interdisciplinary engagement in one of Germany s major academic cities. title: CorpsAfrica Development Associate 2026: Apply for a $55,000–$60,000 Fundraising and Donor Relations Role in Washington, DC
summary: CorpsAfrica is accepting applications for its Development Associate position in Washington, DC , offering an opportunity for early-career professionals interested in fundraising, donor relations, nonprofit management, communications, community development, and international development. The Development Associate will work closely with CorpsAfrica’s Donor Relations Manager and contribute to efforts to expand and strengthen the organisation’s donor base. The successful candidate will support donor cultivation and stewardship, fundraising campaigns, donor events, prospect research, financial reconciliation, and the maintenance of accurate donor information. The position is based in Washington, DC , with a hybrid arrangement requiring two days per week, although remote work may also be considered. The successful applicant should also be willing to travel domestically and internationally for up to 20% of their time. Applications must be submitted by September 30, 2026 . About CorpsAfrica CorpsAfrica is an organisation focused on empowering young Africans to lead community-driven development initiatives within their own countries and across the African continent. The organisation was founded in 2011 by former Peace Corps Volunteer Liz Fanning . The idea behind CorpsAfrica emerged from her experience with young Moroccans who expressed an interest in becoming Peace Corps Volunteers so they could contribute to communities in their own country. At the time, the Peace Corps opportunity was available to Americans serving internationally. CorpsAfrica was subsequently developed around a different model: creating opportunities for young Africans to serve as volunteers and contribute to locally led development across Africa. CorpsAfrica launched its first programme in Morocco in 2013 . Since then, the organisation has expanded significantly across the continent. According to CorpsAfrica, its programmes have operated across countries including: Morocco Senegal Malawi Rwanda Kenya South Africa The Gambia Ghana Côte d’Ivoire Ethiopia The organisation has expanded to 11 countries and has an ambitious long-term objective of eventually reaching all 54 African countries . Hundreds of CorpsAfrica Volunteers have participated in the organisation s programmes, supporting more than 800 community projects . These projects have covered a broad range of community priorities, including: Building wells Constructing schools Developing roads Establishing irrigation systems Creating literacy programmes Supporting vegetable farming Supporting livestock farming Advancing community-led development initiatives The organisation s broader approach centres on enabling communities and local changemakers to identify priorities and participate actively in designing and implementing solutions. About the CorpsAfrica Development Associate Position The Development Associate will support CorpsAfrica as the organisation continues to develop its donor community and strengthen its culture of philanthropy. Rather than concentrating exclusively on fundraising outreach, the position combines donor-facing relationship management with operational fundraising responsibilities . The successful candidate will work closely with the Donor Relations Manager to cultivate, steward, and strengthen relationships with donors. An important part of the position involves ensuring donors receive timely and professional communication while maintaining accurate records of their engagement with CorpsAfrica. The Development Associate will also help identify and qualify potential donors, support donor relations strategies, assist with fundraising events and campaigns, and track and analyse donor activity. This means candidates should be comfortable moving between communication-oriented responsibilities and detailed administrative and data-management work. The Development Associate will be responsible for processing donor receipts and acknowledgements promptly. Timely donor acknowledgement is an important component of nonprofit fundraising because it ensures supporters receive appropriate recognition for their contributions while helping the organisation maintain strong relationships with its donor community. The Associate will also help maintain high-quality donor information within Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud . 2. Donor Data Management Accurate data management will be another important component of the position. The Development Associate will: Enter donor information into relevant systems Update existing donor records Verify donor information Maintain accurate fundraising data Support reporting requirements Help ensure fundraising records remain organised and reliable The role will support both fundraising and finance teams, making attention to detail particularly important. Candidates with experience using donor databases or customer relationship management systems may therefore have relevant experience for this position. 3. Cross-Departmental Collaboration The Development Associate will not work exclusively within one team. Instead, the successful candidate will collaborate with colleagues across different departments and geographical locations. This includes working with: Communications teams Development teams Regional teams Finance colleagues Other stakeholders involved in donor engagement This collaboration will help support donor engagement initiatives, fundraising activities, events, reporting, and organisational campaigns. Because CorpsAfrica operates internationally, applicants should be comfortable collaborating across different cultures and time zones. 4. Responsibilities may include: Event logistics Donor outreach Event coordination Communications Follow-up activities Supporting the overall donor experience Candidates with previous experience in event planning, fundraising events, nonprofit events, stakeholder engagement, or similar activities may find this aspect of the role particularly relevant to their background. 5. Prospect Research Expanding an organisation s donor base requires identifying individuals and organisations that may have an interest in supporting its mission. The Development Associate will support the Donor Relations Manager with researching and qualifying major donor prospects. Tools used for this work may include: WealthEngine Salesforce Prospect research can involve reviewing potential supporters, maintaining accurate information, helping determine whether prospects align with the organisation s fundraising priorities, and supporting future cultivation strategies. Experience with WealthEngine is preferred but is not listed as an absolute requirement. 6. Finance Coordination The Development Associate will also collaborate closely with CorpsAfrica s finance team. This work will help ensure fundraising records and financial systems remain aligned. Responsibilities will include supporting accurate reconciliation and reporting between fundraising and financial systems. Because donor contributions have both fundraising and financial reporting implications, accurate coordination between these systems is an important part of maintaining organisational accountability. Educational Requirements Applicants should hold a Bachelor s degree in a relevant discipline. CorpsAfrica specifically identifies the following fields: Marketing Business Communications Nonprofit management Related disciplines Applicants whose degrees are in closely related fields may also qualify, depending on the relevance of their education and professional experience. Professional Experience Required Candidates should have approximately one to three years of relevant professional experience . Relevant experience may include areas such as: Fundraising Donor relations Development Event planning Nonprofit administration Communications Donor database management Stakeholder engagement Related fields As the position is described as entry level, it could be particularly relevant to early-career professionals who have already developed foundational experience and now want to strengthen their careers in nonprofit development and fundraising. title: Youth Endowment Fund Youth Voice Officer 2026: Apply for a £34,200 Youth Engagement Role in London
